name: Utimutiraja
bio: When the court wants supplies and the Portuguese offer protection, Utimutiraja makes separate bargains. His family still bears the consequences of agreements they did not all make.
notes: fact: Birch describes his household’s enslaved people, competing negotiations and the Portuguese execution of him and three relatives (Birch III, pp. 109–110, 125–131, 143–152)
inference: The seizure, supply and correspondence charges in Birch and the intrigues account in Pires do not establish a single private motive (Pires II, p. 281; people-factions.md §2)
gameplay: Specify protection, demands and supplies separately; deals do not bind his son automatically (people-factions.md §2)
